mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent recessionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side response to demand, which is typically associated with robust economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy in response to a weak labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative policy in weak labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing at a rate of more than 3% year-over-year, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of high FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.
